name: Alabama
notes: The Forestry Commission issues Fire Alerts and the Governor can issue statewide No Burn Orders. Seasonal air-quality rules and local exceptions also apply.

name: Alaska
publisher: Alaska Division of Forestry & Fire Protection and Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation

extraUrls.label: DEC winter open-burning rules and maps

notes: State Forestry generally requires burn permits April 1 through August 31 and can suspend permits by zone or order emergency closures. Alaska DEC restricts open burning in designated parts of Fairbanks North Star Borough and Juneau in winter and can issue separate air quality restrictions. Check your local fire department and land manager for other rules.

name: Arizona
publisher: Arizona Department of Forestry and Fire Management, Pima County, and National Park Service

extraUrls.label: Grand Canyon National Park fire restrictions
Maricopa County air quality burning rules and No Burn Days
Area A boundaries in Maricopa, Pinal and Yavapai counties

notes: The state forestry department covers State Trust lands, and counties, cities, fire districts, tribes and federal agencies issue restrictions for their own areas. Air quality rules also apply, including Maricopa County No Burn Days and summer open-burning limits in parts of Maricopa, Pinal and Yavapai counties.

name: Arkansas
publisher: Arkansas Department of Agriculture, Forestry Division
notes: County judges issue and lift burn bans. The Forestry Division publishes reported county orders on its map. We check signed orders for unincorporated Faulkner County. For other areas, check with your county judge or city fire department. Contact the land manager for rules on public lands. State air-quality rules also apply.

name: California

extraUrls.label: CARB agricultural and prescribed burn decisions

notes: CARB reports agricultural and prescribed burn decisions by air basin. CAL FIRE handles residential permits by unit, and local agencies give final authorization.

name: Colorado
publisher: Local Colorado fire authorities and the Air Pollution Control Division

extraUrls.label: Colorado BLM fire restrictions and closures
El Paso County Sheriff fire information
Larimer County fire danger and restrictions
Estes Valley Fire Protection District restrictions

notes: County sheriffs and commissioners, municipalities, fire districts, and federal land managers can issue restrictions for their own areas. We track some local orders and Denver-area indoor wood-burning advisories. Check your local fire authority, land manager and air-quality rules for the burn location.

name: Connecticut
notes: Town burning officials issue open-burning permits, and DEEP's daily fire danger rating can limit them.

name: Delaware
notes: Delaware bans open burning every year from May 1 to September 30. The State Fire Marshal can issue other bans when conditions are dangerous.

name: District of Columbia
publisher: DC Department of Energy and Environment
notes: District air rules limit open fires across DC. National parks in DC may have separate rules.

name: Florida
notes: Florida counties enact burn bans and the Florida Forest Service reports them on a statewide map. Fireworks bans and yard-debris rules are tracked separately.

name: Georgia
publisher: Georgia Environmental Protection Division and Gwinnett County Fire and Emergency Services

extraUrls.label: Georgia Forestry Commission fire and restrictions map
Georgia Forestry Commission permits and county contacts
Gwinnett Fire Marshal daily burn decision and medical burn zones

notes: Georgia EPD limits certain types of burning in 54 counties May through September and 27 counties October through April. The Georgia Forestry Commission can issue emergency bans, and local fire officials can set additional restrictions, including Gwinnett's daily burn decision.

name: Hawaii
notes: State air rules require permits for most open burning. Counties can issue emergency fire orders.

name: Idaho
publisher: Idaho Department of Lands and Idaho DEQ

extraUrls.label: Kootenai County Fire & Rescue burning rules

notes: Land managers issue fire restrictions by zone, and Idaho DEQ issues separate air-quality restrictions. From May 10 through October 20, check state fire-safety permit requirements. Ask your local fire district, city, county, or Tribe about additional rules for your location.

name: Illinois
notes: Illinois has state open-burning rules, and towns and fire districts issue their own restrictions. There is no statewide list of bans.

name: Indiana
notes: Indiana counties issue burn bans and report them to the Department of Homeland Security. Fire chiefs, cities and towns can add their own restrictions.

name: Iowa
notes: The State Fire Marshal issues burn bans for counties at the request of local fire chiefs. We can only confirm active bans; a county not on the list may still have local rules.

name: Kansas
notes: Kansas counties and fire districts issue burn bans. The Flint Hills smoke plan limits some burning each April.

name: Kentucky

extraUrls.label: Kentucky Division for Air Quality burning rules

notes: County judge-executives and cities can issue local burn bans. The Division of Forestry lists orders reported to it. During spring and fall fire seasons, state law limits daytime burning in or near woods or brush. Check with your county judge-executive or fire department for local orders and exceptions.

name: Louisiana
publisher: Louisiana Department of Agriculture and Forestry
notes: Parishes and the state can issue burn bans in Louisiana, and LDAF maps them by parish. Cities and the State Fire Marshal may have exceptions.

name: Maine
notes: Towns issue open-burn permits in Maine, based on daily fire danger. There is no statewide list of bans.

name: Maryland
notes: Maryland DNR can issue statewide burn bans by emergency order. Counties and towns have their own rules.

name: Massachusetts
notes: Massachusetts allows open burning only in season and only where the local fire department permits it each day.

name: Michigan
notes: The DNR reports debris-burning permit conditions in 49 counties in the Upper Peninsula and northern Lower Peninsula. Use the county dropdown on the DNR map for township details. Contact your local fire department or local government wherever the map refers you to a local issuer. Local ordinances and state air quality rules also apply.

name: Minnesota

extraUrls.label: DNR burning permit rules and exceptions
Permit offices and area maps by county
Superior National Forest alerts and orders

notes: The DNR can suspend permits and restrict open burning in designated areas, including parts of counties. Counties and cities can have their own rules, and Tribal and federal land managers issue separate orders. Check the map for your address and follow the rules of the local authority.

name: Mississippi
notes: Mississippi county boards request burn bans and the Forestry Commission approves them. Each ban has an end date and may have exemptions.

name: Missouri
publisher: Missouri Division of Fire Safety, Show Me Fire and U.S. EPA

extraUrls.label: Show Me Fire’s reported county burn bans
EPA-approved St. Louis metro yard-waste rules
St. Louis County open-burning fact sheet
Wentzville Fire Protection District burning rules

notes: Missouri counties, cities and tax-supported fire protection districts can issue and lift local bans. Show Me Fire publishes reviewed reports. Unreported orders may still apply. The St. Louis metro area has separate rules for burning yard waste. Ask your local fire authority about your address and what you plan to burn.

name: Montana
publisher: Montana DEQ, Montana DNRC and local agencies

extraUrls.label: Montana DEQ open burning seasons and guidance
Participating county permits and daily restrictions

notes: Montana DEQ posts daily fall air-quality limits for open burning in parts of western Montana. County and district fire officials manage local permits and closures. Tribal, state and federal land managers issue separate fire restrictions for their jurisdictions. Check the permit issuer and land manager for your location.

name: Nebraska
notes: Local fire chiefs issue open-burning permits in Nebraska. The state can suspend permits by executive order.

name: Nevada
publisher: Nevada Fire Info, Truckee Meadows Fire Protection District and U.S. Forest Service

extraUrls.label: Nevada Division of Forestry state land restrictions
Nevada open-burning permits and smoke rules
Washoe wood-burning device rules and daily hotline

notes: We track daily pile burning in the Truckee Meadows Fire Protection District in part of Washoe County and a campfire order on mapped National Forest lands in part of Clark County. Local fire authorities and air-quality agencies set separate rules. Check the agency that manages the land for current orders.

name: New Hampshire
publisher: New Hampshire Division of Forests and Lands
notes: Town forest fire wardens issue burn permits in New Hampshire. The state can issue emergency bans.

name: New Jersey
notes: The Forest Fire Service reports temporary campfire and agricultural burning restrictions by division or by county. Forest fire wardens handle state permits, and towns can have their own rules.

name: New Mexico
notes: Counties, State Forestry, tribes and federal land managers issue fire restrictions for their own land in New Mexico.

name: New York
publisher: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation and NYC 311
notes: New York bans residential brush burning March 16 through May 14. Outside that window, DEC requires a written permit for eligible brush burning in designated Fire Towns. NYC has separate rules for open fires and outdoor barbecues. The Governor can issue temporary state or regional bans, and local governments and land managers can set stricter rules. Check the authority for your location before burning.

extraUrls.label: DEC wildfire advisories and burn-ban announcements
DEC Fire Towns and brush-burning permits
NYC Fire Code on open fires

name: North Carolina
publisher: N.C. Forest Service and N.C. Division of Air Quality
notes: The N.C. Forest Service announces state burn bans and lifts. Woodland permits and air-quality burn hours depend on where and what you burn. Check your local fire marshal for local bans, especially within 100 feet of a home that is occupied, and check the county air-quality forecast before burning.

extraUrls.label: Local fire department and fire marshal directory

name: North Dakota
publisher: North Dakota Department of Emergency Services

extraUrls.label: Fire emergency and burn restriction guidance

notes: The governor and local governments can issue burn restrictions. The state map shows reported county, city, tribal and land-manager restrictions, often tied to fire danger or a Red Flag Warning. Check with the authority that covers your location and activity.

name: Ohio
notes: Ohio limits outdoor burning of wood, brush, weeds, grass or rubbish in unincorporated areas from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern in March through May and October through November. The law has exceptions. The State Fire Marshal and local fire officials can issue additional bans. Check with your local fire department and follow Ohio EPA rules.

extraUrls.label: State Fire Marshal's outdoor fire guide (PDF)
Ohio Fire Code on emergency bans

name: Oklahoma
notes: Oklahoma county commissioners issue county burn bans, and the Governor can issue a burn ban for many counties at once. Oklahoma Forestry Services maps both.

name: Oregon
publisher: Oregon DEQ, Oregon Department of Forestry and Lane Regional Air Protection Agency

extraUrls.label: Oregon DEQ open burning rules and address map
Lane County home wood heating advisory
Willamette Valley daily open burning announcement
Tualatin Valley Fire and Rescue outdoor burning
BLM fire restrictions on Oregon public lands

notes: We track Oregon Department of Forestry restrictions on land it protects, Lane County air-quality advisories, and the Willamette Valley backyard burning bulletin for special control areas north of Lane County. Cities, counties, fire districts, Tribes and federal land managers can have their own rules. Check your location and type of burning before lighting a fire.

name: Pennsylvania
publisher: Pennsylvania DCNR and Carroll Valley Borough
notes: County officials can issue temporary bans, and the Governor can issue a statewide proclamation. We track Carroll Valley Borough notices in Adams County and the spring fire-ring and fireplace rule on state forest lands. Check the date on DCNR's county map and ask your county, municipality or land manager about current rules.

name: Rhode Island
notes: Rhode Island DEM can ban fires on state land, and towns set their own rules.

name: South Carolina
publisher: South Carolina Forestry Commission and Department of Environmental Services

extraUrls.label: State Forestry Commission orders and lifts
State bans and Red Flag Fire Alerts
Horry County Fire Rescue open-burning rules

notes: The State Forester or Governor can issue temporary burn bans outside city and town limits. We check the Forestry Commission for current residential yard-debris closures and track state limits on land-clearing and residential construction burns. Check the state notices and your local fire department for other orders and the rules for your location.

name: South Dakota
notes: South Dakota county commissioners issue burn bans. There is no statewide list.

name: Tennessee

extraUrls.label: Tennessee burn permits and seasonal rules
Tennessee air-quality rules for open burning
Shelby County open burning and land clearing

notes: We track temporary holds on state burn permits and the October 15 through May 15 permit season. The Agriculture Commissioner can issue bans in consultation with the State Forester and county mayors, and the Governor can issue regional or statewide bans. Check with your local fire authority for rules and orders that apply to your address.

name: Texas
notes: Texas county judges and commissioners courts issue burn bans and report them to the Texas A&M Forest Service, which updates its list daily.

name: Utah
publisher: Utah Division of Forestry, Fire and State Lands
notes: The state forester issues fire restrictions on state and unincorporated private lands. Cities, tribal governments and federal land managers set rules for their own jurisdictions. County and city fire authorities handle residential burn permits, and Utah DEQ sets separate seasonal and air-quality rules. Check the order for your location.

name: Vermont
publisher: Vermont Department of Forests, Parks and Recreation
notes: Town forest fire wardens issue burn permits in Vermont, and the state can issue broader orders.

name: Virginia
publisher: Virginia Department of Forestry, Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources, and National Park Service

extraUrls.label: Virginia DEQ open burning rules and local ordinances
Shenandoah National Park alerts and conditions
Fairfax County recreational fires and open burning

notes: From February 15 through April 30, Virginia limits when you can start a covered fire near woodland, brushland or dry fields. The Governor can issue emergency orders. Counties, independent cities and land managers can add their own restrictions. Check your local fire marshal and the land manager for your address or burn site.

name: Washington

extraUrls.label: Puget Sound air quality burn ban status
King County fire safety burn bans

notes: Ecology and local clean air agencies issue air quality burn bans. DNR sets fire safety restrictions on land it protects, and counties, fire districts, Tribes, and federal land managers have separate rules. Check the agency for your address and the kind of burning you plan.

name: West Virginia
notes: West Virginia limits outdoor burning hours statewide in spring and fall fire seasons. The Governor can issue emergency bans.

name: Wisconsin
notes: The DNR posts debris-burning permit limits and suspensions for its fire protection areas. Check WisBURN after 9 a.m. Central on the day you plan to burn. Cities, villages and other areas outside DNR protection set their own rules. Ask your local fire department about your address.

extraUrls.label: Wisconsin open burning rules by material
City of Madison burning rules and permits

name: Wyoming
publisher: Wyoming State Forestry Division and Wyoming Office of State Lands and Investments

extraUrls.label: Wyoming air-quality and burn permit rules
Rocky Mountain interagency fire restrictions map

notes: County commissioners issue orders for specific areas, and State Forestry maps the orders it receives. Check the latest order with the county fire warden. Open fires are limited year-round on state trust lands. Towns, fire districts, tribal authorities and federal land managers may have their own rules. Wyoming DEQ has separate air-quality and burn permit requirements.
